title: revert(core): drop the exactOptional parse prototype from #6432
body:
The parse override in `$ZodExactOptional` on main carries a hunk labelled `// OPTION B PROTOTYPE`, merged in #6432. It changes what an exact optional accepts, which #6432 is otherwise not about, and the full suite passes without it.

```ts
z.object({ a: z.exactOptional(z.undefined()) }).safeParse({ a: undefined }); // rejected on main
```

That inner accepts only `undefined`, so the schema can never match when the key is present.

| inner | `{ a: undefined }` on main | after this revert |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `z.string()` | rejected, `expected: "nonoptional"` | rejected, `expected: "string"` |
| `z.coerce.string()` | rejected | accepted |
| `z.any()`, `z.unknown()` | rejected | accepted |
| `z.undefined()`, `z.literal(undefined)` | rejected | accepted |
| `z.string().catch("c")` | rejected | accepted |

Each of those inners accepts `undefined` on its own, so an exact optional wrapping one has no basis to reject it. The rejections also replaced the specific type in the error with `nonoptional`.

Only that hunk is reverted. The `propValues` change from #6432 stays — an omittable slot still claims `undefined` at a discriminator lookup — along with its tests and the compile-side duplicate-value guard.

The absent-key half that the prototype also affected is handled in #6434, in the object layer, without touching what is accepted.

Refs #6432.

> ✅ No new issues found. **Reviewed changes** — a single-hunk revert in `packages/zod/src/v4/core/schemas.ts`, checked against the #6432 commit it reverts, the surrounding object/tuple/compile parse paths, and the open follow-up #6434. - **Drops the `OPTION B PROTOTYPE` hunk from `$ZodExactOptional`** — the parse override goes back to a bare `def.innerType._zod.run(payload, ctx)` delegation. This is a byte-for-byte restoration of the pre-#6432 state, including the original `// Override parse to just delegate (no undefined handling)` comment; diffing against `a38ab4a8` confirms nothing else from that commit is touched. - **The override itself correctly stays** — `$ZodOptional.init` installs a parse that short-circuits on `undefined`, so an exact optional has to replace it to reach the inner at all. - **The rest of #6432 survives** — the `field.optin !== undefined` addition to `propValues` in `$ZodObject`, its discriminated-union test, and the compile-side duplicate-discriminator guard are all untouched, and the `an omittable discriminator claims undefined` test still passes. I ran both revisions to confirm the blast radius. Acceptance changes only for inners that themselves accept `undefined`, and the error for the common case gets *more* specific (`expected: "string"` instead of `expected: "nonoptional"`): | probe | `a38ab4a` | this PR | | --- | --- | --- | | `z.object({ a: z.string().exactOptional() }).parse({ a: undefined })` | `ERR nonoptional` | `ERR string` | | `z.object({ a: z.any().exactOptional() }).parse({ a: undefined })` | `ERR nonoptional` | accepted | | `z.exactOptional(z.any()).parse(undefined)` | `ERR nonoptional` | accepted | Full suite is green locally (7324 passed, 12 skipped); the only failures are the three `@zod/treeshaking` tests that need `pnpm build` first. ### ℹ️ Merging this before #6434 reopens the absent-key window on `main` The prototype was doing a second thing the description only mentions in passing: it was incidentally masking #6236. With it gone, an absent key on a middle-rung inner materializes whatever that inner makes of `undefined` again — `z.object({ a: z.coerce.string().exactOptional() }).parse({})` goes from `{}` back to `{ a: "undefined" }`, `.catch("C")` back to `{ a: "C" }`, and the tuple analog back to `["x", "undefined"]`. That's the pre-#6432 behavior, not a new bug, and #6434 is the real fix — but nothing in the suite pins it in either direction, so the window is invisible to CI.
Technical details ````markdown # Absent-key behavior regresses between #6438 and #6434 ## Affected sites - `packages/zod/src/v4/core/schemas.ts:3746` — removing the prototype restores delegation, so an absent key runs the inner on `undefined` and `handlePropertyResult` assigns the result whenever it is not `undefined`. ## Observed (both revisions run locally) | probe | `a38ab4a` | this PR | | --- | --- | --- | | `z.object({ a: z.coerce.string().exactOptional() }).parse({})` | `{}` | `{ a: "undefined" }` | | `z.object({ a: z.string().catch("C").exactOptional() }).parse({})` | `{}` | `{ a: "C" }` | | `z.tuple([z.string(), z.coerce.string().exactOptional()]).parse(["x"])` | `["x"]` | `["x", "undefined"]` | ## Required outcome - `main` should not ship a release in the state between this revert and #6434. ## Notes - The dependency runs the other way too: #6434's new `optin-ladder.test.ts` cases pin `z.object({ a: z.coerce.string().exactOptional() }).parse({ a: undefined })` to `{ a: "undefined" }`, which only holds once this hunk is gone. So #6438 is a prerequisite for #6434, and #6434 closes the window it opens. - The full suite passes identically with and without the reverted hunk, which is how the prototype rode into `main` in #6432 unnoticed. #6434 adds the pins for both halves; if it stalls, that coverage gap stays open. ````
